title: Double-Crust Apple Pie
summary: A flaky all-butter double crust filled with precooked, gently spiced apples that stay in neat slices and never leave a gap under the lid.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1 cm cubes

ingredients.note: plain cultured sour cream; check the label

ingredients.item: firm apples such as Golden Delicious, Gala or Braeburn (about 8)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: Whisk the 60 g sour cream with the 90 ml ice-cold water. Mix the flour, sugar and salt, then rub or pulse in the butter until the pieces are no bigger than peas, add the sour-cream water and mix until the dough clumps with no dry flour left. Knead briefly, halve, press into 2 discs, wrap and chill 1 h; the acidity of the sour cream keeps the crust tender.

steps.title: Precook the apples
steps.text: Peel, core and cut the apples into 5 mm slices, then toss with the caster sugar, brown sugar, salt and spices in the pot. Cover and cook over medium heat 10-15 min, stirring gently every few minutes, until the slices just bend without breaking. Stir in the cornflour mixed with the lemon juice and simmer 1 min until glossy; off the heat add the zest and vanilla, spread on the tray and cool completely, about 30 min. Cooking first shrinks the apples now rather than in the oven, so no hollow forms under the top crust.

steps.title: Roll the rounds
steps.text: Roll 1 disc to a 30 cm round, ease it into the dish and leave the overhang. Roll the second disc to a 28 cm round for the lid. Keep both cool while you work so the butter stays in flakes.

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan) with a baking tray on the lowest shelf. Pile the cooled apples into the lined dish, leaving most of the syrup behind, lay the top round over, trim both layers to a 1 cm overhang, fold under and crimp. Cut 4 short vents, brush with egg, sprinkle with the 1 tbsp sugar and chill 15 min. Cool filling and chilled pastry mean the crust starts baking before the butter can melt out.

steps.title: Bake hot, then lower
steps.text: Set the pie on the hot tray and bake 20 min, then lower to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and bake 35-45 min more until the crust is deep golden and thick juices bubble through the vents. Cover the edge with foil if it browns too fast. The hot tray crisps the base, and bubbling juices show the cornflour has fully thickened.

steps.title: Cool before slicing
steps.text: Cool on the rack at least 3 h so the filling sets, then slice into 8. Keep at room temperature, loosely covered, for 1 day, or chill up to 4 days and warm slices at 180 °C (160 °C fan) 10 min. Cutting too soon lets the still-liquid juices run out.

tips: A mix of apple varieties gives both soft and firm slices; avoid very soft cooking apples, which collapse.
Common mistake: filling the pie with warm apples. Warm fruit melts the butter in the raw base, so let it cool fully.
Leave most of the syrup in the tray; a little extra makes the base soggy.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep loosely covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge up to 4 days. Freeze whole or in slices up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and warm at 180 °C (160 °C fan) about 10 min.
